method_card.title: Weather, Travel Problems and Transactions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers weather vocabulary, travel problems and transactional language at a tourist information office — all of which are tested across speaking, listening, reading and writing papers.

SpanishEnglish
Hace solIt's sunny
Hace calorIt's hot
Hace fríoIt's cold
Hace buen tiempoThe weather is good
Hace mal tiempoThe weather is bad
Llueve / Está lloviendoIt's raining
Nieva / Está nevandoIt's snowing
Está nubladoIt's cloudy
He perdido mi maleta.I have lost my suitcase.
Me han robado.I have been robbed.
He perdido mi pasaporte.I have lost my passport.
¿Dónde está…?Where is…?
¿A qué hora abre/cierra?What time does it open/close?
¿Puede recomendarme…?Can you recommend…? (formal)

Grammar focus — weather expressions and the perfect tense for travel problems: Weather in Spanish uses hacer + noun: hace calor (literally 'it makes heat'). In the past, use the imperfect for background weather description: hacía mucho frío (it was very cold). For travel problems, the perfect tense (haber + past participle) is natural for recent or ongoing relevance: he perdido mi pasaporte (I have lost my passport). Polite requests at tourist information use ¿Puede…? (Can you…? — usted form).

Model paragraph: Ayer hacía mucho viento y llovía. Por la tarde fui a la oficina de turismo porque he perdido mi pasaporte. El empleado me ayudó y me recomendó una comisaría cerca del centro. (Yesterday it was very windy and it was raining. In the afternoon I went to the tourist information office because I had lost my passport. The employee helped me and recommended a police station near the centre.)
steps: Learn weather expressions with hacer, llueve, nieva, and está nublado
Use imperfect (hacía) for past weather descriptions
Master perfect tense phrases for travel problems: he perdido, me han robado
Practise polite transactional phrases for the tourist information office role-play

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — weather and travel problems appear across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Hacía calor y nadamos en el mar. Fue muy divertido.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hacía calor — note hacía is imperfect (ongoing description of heat). It was hot.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Nadamos = we swam (preterite — completed action). Fue muy divertido = it was great fun (preterite of ser for a completed judgement).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: It was hot and we swam in the sea. It was great fun.

worked_examples.question: Form the past weather description: 'Ayer _____ (hacer) mucho viento y _____ (llover).'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ayer (yesterday) signals the past. Weather in the past is described with the imperfect.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Hacer in the imperfect (3rd person singular) = hacía. Llover (to rain) in the imperfect = llovía.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish weather expressions to their English meaning
Match the Spanish to the English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: en el mar con mis amigos.

gaps.correct_explain: hacía (imperfect) is used for weather descriptions in the past. Hizo (preterite) is also accepted.

wrong.hace: hace is the present tense. Ayer requires a past tense.
wrong.hará: hará is the future tense. Ayer is past.

gaps.correct_explain: nadé is the yo preterite of nadar — a completed action yesterday.

wrong.nadaba: nadaba is the imperfect — for habitual past actions, not a single event yesterday.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: mi pasaporte. Necesito ir a la oficina de turismo.

gaps.rule: Perfect tense — past participle of perder
gaps.correct_explain: perdido is the past participle of perder. He perdido = I have lost (perfect tense).

wrong.perdí: perdí is the preterite (I lost). Both are possible, but he perdido (perfect) is more natural for an ongoing problem.
wrong.pierde: pierde is the present tense (loses/is losing). This is a past event.

bronze.question: What does 'Hacía buen tiempo y fui de compras' mean?
options: The weather was good and I went shopping
The weather is good and I go shopping
The weather will be good and I will go shopping
The weather was bad and I went shopping

bronze.question: What does 'Estaba tomando el sol cuando empezó a llover' mean?
options: I was sunbathing when it started to rain
I sunbathed and then it rained
I will sunbathe if it doesn't rain
I always sunbathe when it's sunny

bronze.source_text: Hacía calor y nadamos en el mar. Fue muy divertido.
model_answers: It was hot and we swam in the sea. It was great fun.

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.audio_text: Hacía sol y nadé en el mar.

bronze.translation: It was sunny and I swam in the sea.

silver.question: Complete the sentence
silver.english: I **was resting** on the beach when it **started** to rain.

gaps.correct_explain: Estaba descansando = I was resting. Past continuous: estar in the imperfect + gerund (-ando for -ar verbs).

wrong.Descansé: Descansé is the preterite (I rested). The English says 'I was resting' — an ongoing background action, so use the past continuous.

gaps.correct_explain: Empezó is the preterite of empezar — a sudden interrupting event.

wrong.empezaba: empezaba is the imperfect. The interrupting action (it started to rain) is a single, sudden event → preterite.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ayer hizo sol y estaba nadado en el mar.
silver.explanation: The past continuous uses the gerund (-ando/-iendo), not the past participle (-ado/-ido). Nadar → nadando (swimming), not nadado (swum — past participle).
silver.translation: Yesterday it was sunny and I was swimming in the sea.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: I was sunbathing when it started to rain.

distractor_labels.tomado: wrong form — tomado is the past participle (used in he tomado). The past continuous needs the gerund: tomando

silver.source_text: It was sunny and I went shopping. I bought some souvenirs.
model_answers: Hacía sol y fui de compras. Compré recuerdos.
hints: to go shopping = ir de compras

silver.question: Listen and type what you hear
silver.audio_text: Estábamos comiendo cuando empezó a llover y fuimos al hotel.
silver.correct_text: Estábamos comiendo cuando empezó a llover y fuimos al hotel.
silver.translation: We were eating when it started to rain and we went to the hotel.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: Last summer the weather was great and I swam in the sea every day. I was sunbathing when it started to rain. In the future I would like to visit a city because I would do sightseeing.
model_answers: El verano pasado hacía muy buen tiempo y nadé en el mar todos los días. Estaba tomando el sol cuando empezó a llover. En el futuro me gustaría visitar una ciudad porque haría turismo.

Check: imperfect for weather (hacía), preterite for single events (nadé, empezó), past continuous (estaba tomando), conditional (me gustaría, haría). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: Every morning we were swimming in the sea and in the afternoon we bought souvenirs.

distractor_labels.nadamos: wrong tense — nadamos is preterite/present; habitual past actions use the imperfect: nadábamos
distractor_labels.compramos: wrong tense — compramos is preterite/present; habitual actions need the imperfect: comprábamos
distractor_labels.las: wrong article — tarde is singular feminine, so use la not las

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a tourist information office in Spain. You need help after a travel problem.

bullets.prompt: Greet the assistant and explain that you have lost your passport.
bullets.model_answer: ¡Buenos días! He perdido mi pasaporte y necesito ayuda, por favor.
bullets.note: greeting + perfect tense (he perdido) + request for help

bullets.prompt: Describe what the weather was like when the problem happened.
bullets.model_answer: Hacía mucho viento y llovía cuando perdí mi pasaporte en la playa.
bullets.note: imperfect for weather (hacía, llovía) + preterite for the event (perdí)

bullets.prompt: Ask the assistant to recommend the nearest police station.
Ask what time the tourist information office opens tomorrow.
bullets.model_answer: ¿A qué hora abre la oficina de turismo mañana?

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking a role play at a tourist information office. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the Spanish grammatically accurate? Check: perfect tense (he perdido), weather imperfect (hacía, llovía), preterite for the event (perdí), polite usted question forms (¿Puede recomendarme?, ¿A qué hora abre?). Award marks out of 10. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in Spanish about a travel problem you had on holiday. Include: what the weather was like, what happened, how you solved the problem, and how you felt.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE Spanish examiner marking extended writing about a travel problem. Mark on: Communication (weather, event, solution, feelings all addressed?), Range of language (imperfect for weather/descriptions, preterite for events, perfect tense for problems, opinion phrases), Accuracy (tense selection, verb forms, accents). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Estaba tomando el sol en la playa cuando empezó a llover y tuvimos que volver al hotel.
gold.correct_text: Estaba tomando el sol en la playa cuando empezó a llover y tuvimos que volver al hotel.
gold.translation: I was sunbathing on the beach when it started to rain and we had to go back to the hotel.

gold.question: Complete the sentence
gold.english: It is important that we look after the environment so that future generations can enjoy travelling.
sentence_parts: el medio ambiente para que las generaciones futuras

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive after es importante que
gaps.correct_explain: cuidemos is the nosotros present subjunctive of cuidar. After es importante que, Spanish requires the subjunctive.

wrong.cuidamos: cuidamos is the present indicative (we look after). After es importante que, the subjunctive is required: cuidemos.
wrong.cuidar: cuidar is the infinitive. You need a conjugated subjunctive form after es importante que.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive of poder after para que
gaps.correct_explain: puedan is the ellos/ellas present subjunctive of poder. After para que, the subjunctive is required.

wrong.pueden: pueden is the present indicative. After para que, use the subjunctive: puedan.
wrong.poder: poder is the infinitive. You need a conjugated subjunctive form after para que.
